question: A shopkeeper expects a gain of 34% on his cost price. If, in a week, his sales proceeds were ₹3,417, what was his profit (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **ratio-unitary** method based on **Selling Price (SP)** percentage.

Given **Gain% = 34%**, so **SP = 134%** of **Cost Price (CP)**.

If 134% ⇒ ₹3,417, then 1% ⇒ 3,417 ÷ 134 = ₹25.5.

**Profit** is 34%, so Profit = 34 × 25.5 = ₹867.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹867.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sales proceeds (SP) = ₹3,417, Gain% = 34%.
**Formulas:** CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 + Gain%] | Profit = SP − CP.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a4c525f0f7775009f12cc9166bf26c071be62ddfa1d07918bcbd83a177569ef.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** be x.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = x + 34% of x = 1.34x.

⇒ 1.34x = 3,417 ⇒ x = 3,417 ÷ 1.34 = ₹2,550.

⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 3,417 − 2,550 = ₹867.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹867.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between SP, CP and Profit

Profit is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise. Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP.

Fractional Method

34% can be written as 34/100 or 17/50. Here, 50 is **CP** and 17 is **Profit**, making **SP** = 67 units.
